title: Onboarding a new hire
summary: A fictional example of use beyond PRs: a cross-department process, from signing the contract to the end of the first month.

nodes.label: Contract signed
nodes.summary: The starting point: once it is signed, the other areas are notified and start preparing for the arrival.

nodes.label: First day
nodes.summary: What the person sees on day one. Everything else in the diagram exists so this day goes well.

nodes.label: Logs in with their credentials
nodes.summary: If IT made it in time, the laptop boots and email works. It is the most visible failure when something runs late.

nodes.label: Welcome session
nodes.summary: An hour with People and culture: how the company works and who to ask about what.

nodes.label: First month
nodes.summary: The weeks in which the person goes from observing to contributing.

nodes.label: Administrative setup
nodes.summary: Everything that has to exist before day one: the person's record, their contract and their payroll.

nodes.label: Create the employee record
nodes.summary: The record is the source of truth for every other system: without it, IT cannot create the accounts.

nodes.label: Add to payroll
nodes.summary: Needs bank and tax details; if they are missing, the first paycheck is delayed.

nodes.label: Onboarding plan
nodes.summary: The script for the first month: sessions, reading and who accompanies them each week.

nodes.label: First-day agenda
nodes.summary: Sent to the person and their manager the week before.

nodes.label: 30-day survey
nodes.summary: Closes the process: what worked and what did not, to improve the next onboarding.

nodes.label: Hardware
nodes.summary: Laptop and peripherals. The purchase lead time is what most often sets the schedule.

nodes.label: Accounts and access
nodes.summary: Email, SSO and the team's tools, with the permissions the manager requests.

nodes.label: SSO account
nodes.summary: Created from the HR record: if the record changes, the account updates itself.

nodes.label: Team permissions
nodes.summary: The specific groups and access for the role. The manager defines them, not IT.

nodes.label: Prepare the arrival
nodes.summary: What the team decides beforehand: first task, onboarding buddy and permissions.

nodes.label: Pick an onboarding buddy
nodes.summary: Someone on the team who is not the manager and answers the small questions.

nodes.label: First real task
nodes.summary: Small and finishable in the first week: it gives an early sense of contributing.

nodes.label: Follow-up
nodes.summary: Weekly one-on-ones during the first month.

edges.label: the record creates the account
edges.summary: The connection that matters most: if the record is late, everything IT does is late.

flows.title: The first day
flows.summary: What has to have happened before 9:00.

steps.title: It all starts with the signature
steps.body_html: Signing the contract notifies People and culture, who open the person's record. Everything else hangs off that record.

steps.title: The record creates the accounts
steps.body_html: What travels: the data in the record. What triggers it: the HR setup. If the record is late, so are the first-day credentials.

steps.title: The team decides what access is needed
steps.body_html: IT does not guess permissions: the manager requests them based on the first task the person will do.

steps.title: 9:00 on the first day
steps.body_html: Three things have to be ready at once: credentials, a laptop and a buddy to welcome them. Miss one and the day starts badly.

steps.title: It closes after 30 days
steps.body_html: The process ends with a survey for the person. Their answers improve the onboarding plan for the next hire.
